destinations.name: Lisbon
facts: Lisbon is one of the oldest cities in western Europe and was almost destroyed by an earthquake in 1755.
The recipe of the pastel de nata was first made by monks in Belém. It is still a secret.
The yellow trams of Lisbon are over 90 years old, and many climb slopes of more than 10 per cent.

destinations.name: Marrakech
facts: Marrakech is called the Red City because of the colour of its walls, built from local clay.
The Jemaa el-Fna square is recognised by UNESCO for its living traditions: storytellers, musicians and food stalls.
Moroccan mint tea is poured from a height to make it foam. A good host pours it high.

destinations.name: Istanbul
facts: Istanbul is the only major city in the world built on two continents, Europe and Asia.
The Grand Bazaar has more than 4,000 shops and is one of the oldest covered markets in the world.
The dome of Hagia Sophia has stood since the year 537.

destinations.name: Petra
facts: Petra was unknown to the western world until 1812, when a Swiss explorer disguised himself to reach it.
The Treasury is carved straight into the cliff and is about 40 metres high.
The Nabataeans lived in the desert by catching every drop of rain in channels and cisterns.

destinations.name: Paro
facts: Bhutan measures its progress in Gross National Happiness, not only in money.
Paro airport is among the most demanding in the world: only a small group of pilots are trained to land here.
Bhutan absorbs more carbon than it produces. Forest covers more than two thirds of the country.

destinations.name: Siem Reap
facts: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world. It was built in about 30 years, in the 12th century.
Ta Prohm was left almost as the jungle claimed it. It appears in the film Tomb Raider.
Every year the Tonlé Sap river changes direction: it flows towards the lake in the dry season and away from it in the rainy season.

destinations.name: Kyoto
facts: Kyoto was the capital of Japan for more than a thousand years, from 794 to 1868.
The city has about 1,600 Buddhist temples and 400 Shinto shrines.
Geiko is the Kyoto word for a geisha.

destinations.name: Maldives
facts: The Maldives is the lowest country on Earth: its highest point is only a few metres above the sea.
More than 99 per cent of the Maldives is sea. It has about 1,190 islands.
Many Maldivian islands sit on top of ancient coral rings called atolls.

destinations.name: Kigali
facts: Rwanda is called the Land of a Thousand Hills, and Kigali is built across several of them.
Plastic bags have been banned in Rwanda since 2008, and the last Saturday of the month is a community clean-up day.
About a thousand mountain gorillas live in the wild, and a large part of them live in the volcanoes of Rwanda.

destinations.name: Cape Town
facts: Table Mountain is one of the oldest mountains on Earth, and its flat top is often covered by a "tablecloth" of cloud.
African penguins live on the beaches near Cape Town.
Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in prison on Robben Island.

destinations.name: Seychelles
facts: The coco de mer palm has the heaviest seed in the world: up to 25 kilos.
Aldabra giant tortoises can live for more than 150 years.
The Seychelles has 115 islands, and the oldest are granite, not coral.

destinations.name: Marrakech farewell
facts: Marrakech is called the Red City because of the colour of its walls, built from local clay.
The Jemaa el-Fna square is recognised by UNESCO for its living traditions: storytellers, musicians and food stalls.
Moroccan mint tea is poured from a height to make it foam. A good host pours it high.

options.name: Alfama walking tour
options.difficulty_note: About 2.5 km on steep, cobbled streets with many steps and no lift. Cobbles are slippery when wet.
options.description: Today we get lost on purpose in the oldest quarter of Lisbon. Narrow lanes tumble down towards the Tagus, tiled facades shine in the sun, and somewhere above us a fado singer is practising. We climb to viewpoints over the red roofs and the river, and stop for a coffee and a warm custard tart. Lisbon at its most Lisbon.
options.bring: Cobbled streets: comfortable shoes with grip. The sun can be strong: a hat.
options.accessibility: About 2.5 km on steep, cobbled streets with many steps and no lift. Cobbles are slippery when wet. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Tram 28 and viewpoints
options.difficulty_note: Mostly seated. The vintage tram is crowded and its seats are hard. Short, flat walks between viewpoints.
options.description: Today we ride the yellow tram that rattles through the hills of Lisbon, squeezing past walls and climbing streets that look impossible. At three viewpoints we step off to see the city spread out below us, terracotta and white, all the way to the river. It is the most charming way to meet a city.
options.bring: Cobbled streets: comfortable shoes with grip. The sun can be strong: a hat.
options.accessibility: The historic trams have a high step and narrow seating, and the ride is bumpy. Viewpoints are reached by short slopes with a few steps.

options.name: Sintra palaces
options.description: Today we step into a fairy tale in the hills above Lisbon. In Sintra, mist drifts between pink and yellow palaces, towers and hidden gardens, and the royal families of Portugal once escaped the summer heat. Our guide leads us through painted rooms and secret tunnels.
options.accessibility: Steep paths between the sites and many stairs inside the palaces, with no lift. Cobbled courtyards. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Tile painting workshop
options.description: Today we pick up a brush and join a Lisbon tradition that is seven hundred years old. In a workshop, a master painter shows us how azulejos are made, and we paint our own tile in blue and white. You take home something no shop can sell.

options.name: Belém and pastel de nata tasting
options.description: Today we visit the place where the great explorers set sail. In Belém, a tower and a monument remember the voyages that changed the world, and then, at the original bakery, we taste the pastel de nata, warm from the oven, with cinnamon. A little history, a little sugar, a lot of joy.

options.name: Tagus sunset sail
options.difficulty_note: On a sailing boat: stepping on and off the boat and a few steps below deck. The boat can move; people prone to seasickness may want to take a tablet beforehand.
options.description: Today the evening belongs to the river. A small sailing boat carries us onto the Tagus at golden hour, the city glows pink behind us, and a glass of wine appears as the sun slips towards the Atlantic. There is no better way to say goodbye to Lisbon.
options.bring: It can be windy and wet on the water: a light jacket and soft-soled shoes.
options.accessibility: Stepping on and off the boat is needed; the crew will help. Not suitable for wheelchairs.

options.name: Medina orientation walk
options.description: Today we learn to read the maze. With a local guide, we step into the medina of Marrakech through an old gate and discover its secret logic: where the dyers work, where the spice sellers sit, and how to find our way home. By the end, the labyrinth feels like a village.

options.name: Hammam and spa
options.description: Today we do what Moroccans have done for centuries. In the warm steam of a traditional hammam, we are scrubbed and rinsed with black soap, then wrapped in a towel and given mint tea. Afterwards, a massage with argan oil. We leave feeling like new travellers.

options.name: Atlas Mountains village visit
options.description: Today we drive into the Atlas to a village that seems far from the world. Mud-brick houses climb a hillside, children wave from the paths, and a Berber family opens its doors for tea and fresh bread. We walk between orchards, listening to the stories of mountain life.

options.name: Majorelle Garden
options.description: Today we enter a garden painted in a blue found nowhere else. Created by a French artist and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent, the Majorelle Garden mixes cobalt walls, tall cacti and quiet pools, and we wander along its paths in the cool shade. A pocket of calm in the middle of Marrakech.

options.name: Souk treasure hunt with a guide
options.description: Today we turn the souks into a game. With a local guide, we look for the best lanterns, leather, spices and carpets, learn how to bargain with a smile, and discover where artisans still work as they did centuries ago. Everyone comes back with a story, and a bag.

options.name: Moroccan cooking class
options.description: Today we roll up our sleeves in a Moroccan kitchen. We choose vegetables at the market, learn to layer a tagine and shape a pastilla, and then sit down together to eat what we cooked. You leave knowing how to make a meal that tastes like Marrakech.

options.name: Bosphorus boat
options.description: Today we sail between two continents. A boat carries us up the Bosphorus past Ottoman palaces, wooden mansions and fortresses, with Europe on one side and Asia on the other, and the call to prayer drifting over the water. Istanbul looks different from the sea.

options.name: Old City walk
options.description: Today we walk through two thousand years in one morning. Between the Hippodrome, the Blue Mosque and quiet back streets, our guide tells how an empire grew from this hilltop, and we stop at a tea garden to watch the ferries cross the water. Istanbul in a single breath.

options.name: Topkapi Palace and Hagia Sophia
options.description: Today we step into the heart of empires. At Topkapi Palace, sultans lived among courtyards, treasures and a harem full of secrets. Then, at Hagia Sophia, we stand beneath a dome that has been looking down on the city for 1,500 years. Gold, marble and light.

options.name: Spice market food walk
options.description: Today we follow our noses. In the Spice Market, we taste Turkish delight, dried figs, fresh cheese, simit and strong coffee, and learn how each stall tells the story of a trade route. Come hungry. We will not let you go away disappointed.

options.name: Grand Bazaar with a guide
options.description: Today we enter one of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world. Over 4,000 shops sit beneath painted vaults, and with our guide, we find the best lamps, ceramics and jewellery, and learn how to bargain over a glass of tea. It is a story with every step.

options.name: Hammam
options.description: Today we slip into an Ottoman bathhouse. Under a marble dome, warm steam loosens our muscles, an attendant scrubs and foams us with a cloth, and a cup of tea follows. It is a ritual older than the city's mosques, and it feels like a gift.

options.name: Art galleries of Karaköy
options.description: Today we discover the creative side of Istanbul. In Karaköy, old warehouses have become galleries, studios and cafes, and we wander the streets with a local who knows every artist. A different city, young and bold.

options.name: Petra by Night
options.description: Today we walk into a story told by candlelight. The Siq, the narrow canyon that leads to Petra, glows with thousands of candles, and at the end, the Treasury appears out of the dark. We sit on the ground, hear a Bedouin musician play, and drink sweet tea under the stars. Few experiences are so quiet and so magical.
options.accessibility: The Siq is 1.2 km on uneven sandy paving, walked in the dark by candlelight. Seating at the Treasury is on mats on the ground. Not suitable for wheelchairs. A horse or cart is available for part of the way.

options.name: Petra main trail to the Treasury
options.description: Today we follow the classic route into Petra. The path leads down through the narrow Siq to the Treasury, which seems to grow out of the rock, and onward along the Street of Facades. Plenty of time for photos, tea and silence.

options.name: Monastery hike (challenging)
options.difficulty_note: About 800 stone steps up to the Monastery, over roughly 1 hour 30 minutes, in the heat of the day on exposed ground. Very little shade. Not suitable for anyone with heart, knee or balance problems.
options.description: Today we climb 800 rock-cut steps to the largest monument of Petra. The Monastery, taller than the Treasury, waits at the top, and the view from the cliff behind it stretches towards Wadi Araba. A hard climb, a huge reward.
options.bring: The sun is strong and there is little shade: hat and sturdy closed shoes. Keep to the paths and do not climb on the monuments.
options.accessibility: Not suitable for wheelchairs or walking aids, or for guests with heart, knee or balance problems. Please speak to your guide before choosing it.

options.name: Petra by horse cart
options.difficulty_note: Seated in a cart on a rough track: bumpy, with no seat belts. Getting in and out needs a big step.
options.description: Today we see Petra in comfort. A horse cart carries us along the main trail as far as the Treasury, so we arrive fresh and can enjoy the monuments without the long walk. A gentle way to meet a wonder.
options.bring: The sun is strong and there is little shade: hat and sturdy closed shoes. Keep to the paths and do not climb on the monuments.
options.accessibility: Mostly level and gentle: suitable for most guests, including those who walk slowly. Tell your guide if you use a wheelchair or a walker and we will check access for you.

options.name: Wadi Rum jeep safari
options.description: Today we drive into the Valley of the Moon. In a jeep we cross red sand between towering sandstone cliffs, stop at a Bedouin camp for sweet tea and watch the sun set across a desert that looks like Mars. T. E. Lawrence called it vast, echoing and godlike.

options.name: Little Petra walk
options.description: Today we visit the quiet side of Petra. A short walk takes us through the narrow canyon of Little Petra, where Nabataean traders once rested, and a Bedouin family serves tea in the shade. Calm, quiet and beautiful.

options.name: Paro town and dzong
options.description: Today we explore Paro, the valley where Bhutan's only international airport sits among rice terraces. We cross a wooden bridge to the great dzong, a fortress of whitewashed walls and carved balconies, and wander the town's main street, where every house is painted with symbols of luck.

options.name: Hot stone bath
options.description: Today we soak the way Bhutanese farmers do. Stones heated in a wood fire are dropped into a wooden tub, the water turns warm and fragrant with mugwort, and the cold of the mountains disappears. A slow evening under the stars.

options.name: Tiger's Nest hike (challenging)
options.difficulty_note: About 10 km round trip with a climb of roughly 900 m, starting at 2,600 m above sea level, so the air is thin. Around 700 uneven steps near the top. Allow 4 hours up and 2 hours down. Not recommended with heart or knee problems or a fear of heights: some stretches are narrow with a drop beside the path. Horses can carry you part of the way up.
options.description: Today we climb to one of the most breathtaking temples ever built. Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest, clings to a cliff 900 metres above the Paro valley, and we reach it on foot through pine forests, prayer flags and a stairway cut into the rock. Hard work. Unforgettable reward. A teahouse waits halfway.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees. No photographs inside the monastery, and bags are left at the entrance. A warm layer: it is cold at height.
options.accessibility: A climb of about 800 m of height over roughly 3 to 4 hours, with some 700 steps near the top and no handrails in places. A pony can help for the first part (extra cost). Not suitable for wheelchairs or for guests with heart or knee problems.

options.name: Tiger's Nest viewpoint (easy)
options.difficulty_note: A gentle 2 km walk with a climb of about 150 m on a wide, even path, at 2,600 m above sea level. No steps. A bench every few minutes. A tea stop at the cafeteria, with the monastery in view across the gorge.
options.description: Today we see the Tiger's Nest without the climb. A short walk leads to a viewpoint facing the monastery, where it hangs from the cliff in the morning light, and we sip tea in the cafeteria with the greatest view in Bhutan. Easy steps, a legendary sight.
options.bring: Cover shoulders and knees. No photographs inside the monastery, and bags are left at the entrance. A warm layer: it is cold at height.
options.accessibility: A gentle walk of 15 minutes on a wide path with a short slope. The cafeteria has a terrace with benches and one step at the entrance. Easy for most guests.

options.name: Archery with local teams
options.difficulty_note: Mostly standing on grass. A short walk of about 500 m to the archery ground. You stand for up to two hours, in the sun or wind, so bring a hat. You can watch from a chair if you prefer, and still join the lunch and the singing.
options.description: Today we try Bhutan's national sport. Local teams show how the targets, 140 metres away, are hit with traditional bows, with singing, dancing and teasing for every miss. We join the game, laugh a lot and probably miss, too.
options.bring: Comfortable closed shoes. A sun hat in summer.
options.accessibility: Some steps or uneven ground. Guests with limited mobility should speak to their guide before choosing this tour.

options.name: Farmhouse lunch and butter tea
options.description: Today we are guests in a Bhutanese farmhouse. Under painted wooden beams, the family serves red rice, chilli and cheese, and a cup of salty butter tea, and shows us how life runs in the valley. Simple food, warm welcome.

options.name: Meditation with a monk
options.description: Today we sit in silence. A monk guides us through a short meditation in a quiet temple room, explains how Buddhist practice shapes daily life in Bhutan, and answers our questions. We leave a little calmer, perhaps a little changed.

options.name: Angkor Wat sunset
options.description: Today we watch the sun go down on the largest religious monument on Earth. The towers of Angkor Wat turn gold, then rose, then silhouette against the sky, and the moat reflects it all. A quiet, glowing end to the day.

options.name: Angkor Wat sunrise and Bayon
options.description: Today we rise in the dark to see Angkor Wat appear out of the night. As the sky turns pink behind the five towers, a hush falls over the crowd, and later we visit the Bayon, where more than 200 stone faces smile at us. A morning to remember.

options.name: Ta Prohm by tuk-tuk
options.description: Today we travel like locals. A tuk-tuk takes us through the forest to Ta Prohm, where the roots of giant trees wrap around fallen stones, and we wander among them in the green light. The jungle has won, and it is beautiful.

options.name: Floating village boat trip
options.description: Today we glide onto Tonlé Sap, the great lake of Cambodia. Houses, schools and shops float on the water, and children paddle to class in basins. We watch a life shaped by the rising and falling of the lake.

options.name: Artisans workshop visit
options.description: Today we meet the hands that keep Khmer art alive. In a workshop, young artisans carve stone, paint silk and shape silver, and we see how a craft nearly lost becomes a future. Watch, ask, and take a piece home.

options.name: Gion evening walk
options.description: Today we walk through Kyoto as the lanterns light. In the narrow lanes of Gion, wooden teahouses glow, and with luck, a geiko hurries past on her way to an appointment. Our guide explains the rules of an old world that still survives.

options.name: Tea ceremony
options.description: Today we slow right down. In a tatami room, a tea master prepares a bowl of matcha with movements that have barely changed in five hundred years, and we learn to receive it. A lesson in attention and calm.

options.name: Fushimi Inari early walk
options.description: Today we walk through a tunnel of ten thousand vermilion gates. Early, before the crowds, the paths of Fushimi Inari wind up the forested mountain, past fox statues and small shrines, in a silence broken only by birds. One of the most beautiful walks in Japan.

options.name: Arashiyama bamboo grove
options.description: Today we walk into a green cathedral. In Arashiyama, bamboo stems rise thirty metres above us, the light turns the colour of jade, and the wind makes the leaves whisper. We continue to a quiet temple garden and a riverside tea stop.

options.name: Kinkaku-ji and Zen garden
options.description: Today we see the Golden Pavilion, a Zen temple covered in gold leaf that glows in its own reflection. Then, at a nearby garden, we sit before raked gravel and stones and learn to look. A morning of beauty and stillness.

options.name: Sake brewery visit
options.description: Today we follow rice to the glass. In a family brewery older than most countries, a master explains how water, rice and patience make sake, and then we taste, sip by sip, and learn what we like. Kanpai!

options.name: Welcome beach session
options.description: Today we arrive in paradise and do nothing at all. White sand, clear water, a drink in hand and the whole group together on the beach. A slow, easy hello to the Maldives.

options.name: Snorkel with marine biologist
options.difficulty_note: In the sea for about 1 hour 30 minutes. Calm water, but you must be comfortable swimming in open water. A life vest is provided.
options.description: Today we swim with an expert. A marine biologist leads us over a living reef, pointing out the corals, the parrotfish and the hidden creatures we would never spot alone. By the end, we understand what we are looking at.
options.bring: Swimsuit and a towel. Reef-safe sun cream only. Touching the coral is not allowed.
options.accessibility: You step into the water from the boat; floating aids are provided. Please tell your guide about any health condition.

options.name: Scuba discovery dive
options.difficulty_note: Includes a medical questionnaire and a short training in shallow water before the dive. You must be able to swim and have no breathing problems. Not for those who feel uneasy in closed or deep places.
options.description: Today we take our first breaths underwater. With an instructor at our side, we sink slowly to eight metres, hover above the coral and watch fish drift past as if we belonged. No experience needed, only curiosity.
options.bring: Swimsuit and a towel. Reef-safe sun cream only. Touching the coral is not allowed.
options.accessibility: Not suitable for wheelchairs or walking aids, or for guests with heart, knee or balance problems. Please speak to your guide before choosing it.

options.name: Sandbank picnic
options.difficulty_note: A short boat ride, then a few steps in shallow water to reach the sand. No shade except the umbrellas we bring.
options.description: Today a boat takes us to an island that appears and disappears with the tide. A sandbank, white and tiny, in the middle of the ocean, with a picnic in the shade and our feet in the water. The most beautiful lunch of the trip.
options.bring: Comfortable closed shoes. A sun hat in summer.
options.accessibility: Mostly level and gentle: suitable for most guests, including those who walk slowly. Tell your guide if you use a wheelchair or a walker and we will check access for you.

options.name: Sunset dolphin cruise
options.description: Today we sail out at golden hour, scanning the waves for fins. Spinner dolphins leap and twist beside the boat, the sky turns orange, and the whole group falls silent. A magical end to the day.

options.name: Spa afternoon
options.description: Today is for you. A long massage, warm oils and the sound of the sea, followed by a quiet rest in a hammock. Nothing to do but breathe out.

options.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
options.description: Today we visit the place where Rwanda remembers. The memorial tells the story of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi with honesty and dignity, through photographs, testimonies and gardens. It is a quiet, moving morning, and a way to understand how the country rebuilt itself.

options.name: Gorilla trekking (permit)
options.description: Today we trek into the misty volcanoes to meet the mountain gorillas. Guided by trackers, we walk through bamboo and wet forest until we find a family, and for one hour we sit a few metres away, watching them eat, play and look back at us. Few moments in life are like this.

options.name: Golden monkey trek
options.description: Today we walk into the bamboo forest to find the golden monkey, one of the rarest primates in Africa. They leap, tumble and chatter above us, and the volcanoes rise in the background. A joyful, easier trek.

options.name: Kigali city and markets
options.description: Today we discover a clean, green and surprising capital. We wander through markets full of colour, taste local fruit and coffee, and learn how Kigali became one of the most welcoming cities in Africa.

options.name: Imigongo art cooperative
options.description: Today we meet the women who paint with cow dung. Imigongo is a Rwandan art form of bold black, red and white spirals, and in a cooperative, we watch the patterns take shape and try our own. Beautiful work with a beautiful purpose.

options.name: Coffee farm visit
options.description: Today we follow Rwandan coffee from the hillside to the cup. We walk among the bushes, pick ripe red cherries, see them washed and dried, and finish with a tasting of the freshest brew we will ever drink.

options.name: Table Mountain cable car
options.description: Today we rise above Cape Town. A rotating cable car lifts us to the flat top of Table Mountain, where fynbos flowers bloom, dassies sunbathe and the whole coast spreads below. On a clear day, you can see forever.

options.name: Bo-Kaap walk
options.description: Today we walk the brightest streets in Cape Town. In the Bo-Kaap, houses are painted in pink, turquoise and yellow, and our guide tells the story of the Cape Malay community that made this hillside home. We finish with a spiced snack.

options.name: Cape Point and penguins
options.description: Today we drive to the edge of a continent. At Cape Point, cliffs plunge into the meeting of two oceans, baboons watch from the rocks, and on a nearby beach, African penguins waddle through the surf. Wild, windy and unforgettable.

options.name: Winelands tasting
options.description: Today we roll through the Cape Winelands. Between mountains and vines, we visit estates older than most nations, taste their finest wines and share a long lunch in the sun. A feast for the senses.

options.name: Robben Island
options.description: Today we visit the island where Nelson Mandela spent eighteen years. A former prisoner guides us through the cells and the quarry, and tells the story in his own words. It is a powerful, moving visit.

options.name: Township food tour
options.description: Today we eat our way through a township. With a local host, we taste home cooking, meet the families who prepare it and learn the stories behind every dish. Warm, generous and full of flavour.

options.name: Beach and welcome drinks
options.description: Today we arrive in a place that looks like a dream. Granite boulders, soft white sand and turquoise water, and a cold drink waiting at sunset. We gather on the beach, and the trip slows to island time.

options.name: Vallée de Mai palm forest
options.description: Today we walk into a prehistoric forest. In the Vallée de Mai, giant coco de mer palms shade the trail, and the world's biggest seeds hang above us. Black parrots call in the leaves, and our guide tells the strange story of this UNESCO treasure.

options.name: Island hopping by boat
options.description: Today we hop across the Seychelles by boat. We land on tiny islands with fine sand, swim in clear lagoons, and walk past granite boulders sculpted by time. Each stop looks more beautiful than the last.

options.name: Snorkel at Anse Lazio
options.description: Today we slip into the water at one of the most beautiful beaches on Earth. Anse Lazio's calm bay is full of fish, and a few steps from the sand we float above rocks, corals and shoals of colour. Simply magical.

options.name: Giant tortoise sanctuary
options.description: Today we meet creatures that have seen centuries pass. At the sanctuary, giant tortoises, some over a hundred years old, plod through the grass and munch on leaves, and we learn how they survive on these islands. Slow, gentle and ancient.

options.name: Creole cooking class
options.description: Today we learn to cook the island way. With a local chef, we grate coconut, simmer fish in spices and make a fresh curry, and then sit down together to eat what we have made. The Seychelles on a plate.

options.name: Farewell brunch in the palm grove
options.description: Today we end the journey under the palms. A long, slow brunch in a Marrakech garden, with the whole group and the expedition team, sharing the moments we loved most. One table, one trip, one story.

options.name: Final shopping with a guide
options.description: Today we bring home a piece of the journey. With a local guide, we visit the best workshops and stalls, find lanterns, leather and spices, and learn how to bargain with a smile. A last adventure in the souks.

options.name: Farewell gala dinner
options.description: Tonight we celebrate the whole journey. Dress up, raise a glass, and share the stories, the photos and the laughs that made this trip ours. A fitting last night.
